Sofia (Sales): Hey team — my Q1 bonus posted on 2026-11-01 but it's showing a flat supplemental US tax withholding instead of Quebec payroll tax. I moved to Montreal on 2026-10-10 and updated my address in Ripley on 10/11. Can this be fixed?
Nina (People Ops): cc @Omar @Alicia. Sofia, did you complete the provincial tax form / Quebec TP-1015.3 enrolment? Also when was the bonus paid in relation to the move?
Sofia (Sales): Bonus payrun was 2026-11-01 (pr-20261101). I filled the Quebec enrolment on 10/12 but payroll confirmation said activation was pending. I have lease + utility dated 10/15 if that helps.
Omar (Payroll): Thanks. System defaulted supplemental rate because the bonus went through the US payroll run and Qc enrolment wasn't active at cutoff. We can request a reversal and reissue under Canadian payroll if residency/tax enrollment supports it. Need proof of move and confirmation of activation timestamp.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): High-level: Canada (QC) generally taxes employment income where the employee is resident. If residency started before pay date, PAYE/QC should apply. Retroactive reallocation is possible but we need to verify cutoffs and whether CRA/Revenu Québec accept amended source deductions. We'll consult our Canadian payroll advisor.

Omar (Payroll): Action plan: 1) Submit reversal request for pr-20261101 to external payroll advisor (submitted). 2) If approved, reissue bonus under CA/QC payroll with provincial withholding and adjust employer contributions. 3) If denied, coordinate US refund path and Finance advance option.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): Scheduling consult with Canadian advisor tomorrow. If Revenu Québec allows correction, we'll file amended source deduction returns and issue a corrected statement. Note that exchange rate and RRSP/CPP considerations may matter.
